focus: Check completeness: per-runtime silent-wrong-result classes and the command-string-detectable predicates for each, including the pi --offline gap and the budget-vs-timeout predicate
noveltyJustification: The per-runtime class inventory and the twelve proposed predicates are new; the devin accept-edits failure was a documented packet fact now joined to its missing detector.
keyQuestions: For each cli-* runtime, which dispatch mistakes produce a silent wrong result rather than an error?

summary: Per-runtime inventory: nine silent classes are command-detectable and unenforced (pi --offline, hermes file toolset/provider/source/-z/budget, opencode --dir, cursor auto-model, claude/codex model pinning, devin accept-edits).
Twelve check predicates are specified in the iteration file, matching the registry's satisfier style, for hermes (5), pi (2), opencode (1), cursor (1), claude (1), codex (1), devin (1).

Pi's --offline flag is mandatory in the builder ('hangs for minutes on startup network probes') but has no hard rule and no check; an ad-hoc pi -p can hang in the slow-model shape with every declared rule satisfied.
Hermes provider pinning, --source tool, and the top-level -z ban are all command-string detectable with no roster data; -z is the only form the packet expressly never uses.
Budget-shorter-than-work is decidable only when both numbers co-appear; the predicate compares --run-budget against a timeout wrapper minus the 60s margin the builder already uses.

Model-allowlist checks need roster tables; the repo already duplicates four rosters between executor-config.ts and fanout-run.cjs, so a third copy in the hook engine would be a new drift site — derive from the single config instead.
Non-detectable classes: model capability vs task, prompt quality, credential state, task-dependent toolset adequacy, and the devin task-intent half of the accept-edits case.

Devin --permission-mode accept-edits is the one fully documented silent-wrong-result with no detector: spends the whole budget exploring, writes nothing, exits 0; the flag is command-visible, hence an advisory predicate is implementable.
